result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days. They default to 30, and you can set them at registration and change them later. The full offline suite passes (176 test classes, no failures). Nothing is committed.

What changed:
- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30`, with a check that it is not negative.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `paymentTermsDays` component. The existing 5-argument constructor defaults it to 30 (`STANDARD_PAYMENT_TERMS_DAYS`), so the many existing call sites still compile.
- **`SupplierStore.java`**: create and update write the terms. The shared select and group-by lists include the column, so all four listings (all, by country, by minimum rating, by id) return it. The single-supplier-per-category query also selects it.
- **`Rows.java`**, **`PurchaseOrderStore.java`**, **`StockStore.java`**: read the column wherever a supplier is built from a row, so the purchased-quantity and reorder-suggestion results carry the real terms too.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: new tests for the default of 30, the 45-then-14 renegotiation shown in every listing, and rejection of negative terms.

Things to be aware of:
- Because of the 5-argument constructor, an `update` made with it resets the terms to 30. `DemoScenario` does this for Nordic Supply; it had 30 days anyway, so the demo output is unchanged. Any new caller that updates a supplier should pass the terms explicitly.
- I did not add a UI or CLI command, because the repo has none for suppliers; registration and renegotiation go through `SupplierStore`.
